newsitem.title: USA: Ore. review of Enron, PGE merger deadlocked.
newsitem.headline: Ore. review of Enron, PGE merger deadlocked.

text.p: With neither side willing to budge, an Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC) settlement conference on the proposed merger of Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co has been delayed to mid-February.
"There will no longer be a conference, but the settlement process is continuing," Gary Foster, a spokesman for Enron said.

Parties involved in reviewing the merger began the three-day conference Wednesday, but it was brought to a halt Friday when staff of the OPUC decided there was no chance of reaching a compromise, according to attendees.
Last week, the staff issued a preliminary review approving the merger as long as several conditions, including a multi-year rate cut, were implemented.

Enron and PGE officials said they questioned the staff's analysis that the utility's rates should be cut $47.4 million annually for four years after the merger and by $11.2 million per year until PGE's next rate case.
The Citizens' Utility Board of Oregon, which had also conditionally agreed to the merger, supports the staff position on the rate cut, said spokesman Jason Eisdorfer.
The OPUC staff was scheduled to make a final recommendation January 31, but that has been cancelled, Enron's Foster said.
Other parts of the merger review schedule have not been redetermined, but the March 17 deadline for a decision by the Oregon commission is still in place, he added.
